question: Your pay rises exactly as fast as prices. Why can you still end up able to buy less?
answer: Because the tax lines don't rise with you. The UK's tax-free allowance has been £12,570 since 2021. On £30,000, a 5% rise lifts income tax by about 8.6%, so take-home pay grows only about 4.5%, behind prices. Economists call it fiscal drag: every year of inflation quietly taxes more of each pay packet.
move: A limit written in money tightens every year nobody updates it.
ask: Which limits in my life are written in money and never updated?

start.text: Pay up 5%, prices up 5%. You still end up a little poorer.
